newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe silent on reshuffle, poll rumours.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe silent on reshuffle, poll rumours.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe declined to comment on Wednesday on rumours that President Jacques Chirac might be considering a cabinet reshuffle or early parliamentary elections.

"Oh no, I cannot comment," he told reporters after an unusually brief weekly cabinet meeting when asked about persistent rumours that Chirac might order a reshuffle or bring forward elections to the National Assembly due in March 1998.
A reshuffle, the second since Chirac came to power in 1995, would enable the government to streamline itself ahead of the elections.

It might allow reconciliation with some leading centre-right politicians whose ties with Chirac soured when they backed his conservative rival, ex-prime minister Edouard Balladur, in the 1995 presidential elections.
By calling an early election, Chirac might hope to renew the favourable centre-right majority for the remainder of his seven-year term.
It would also help avoid a collision between the election timetable and European Union plans to select countries early in 1998 to take part in a single European currency from 1999.
